meta.title: Services — CDMCORP Construction & Project Management Consultants
meta.description: Six services: project management, contract administration, superintendent services, feasibility studies, tender & procurement, risk & quality management. NSW wide.

intro.headline: Six services. Client-side.
intro.lede: CDMCORP acts for the owner, developer, or principal — never for the builder. Every engagement is scoped in writing before we start.

items.name: Project Management
items.trigger: End-to-end, on the owner's side of the table.
items.what: Client-side project management from initial planning through to handover. Programme oversight, cost tracking, consultant coordination, principal reporting, and stakeholder management across the full project lifecycle.
items.when: You need a single project manager accountable to you — not the builder — running the project as an extension of your own team.
items.deliverable: Weekly progress reporting, monthly cost and programme dashboards, risk register maintained live, and a complete document register at handover.

items.name: Contract Administration
items.what: Full contract administration under AS 4000, AS 4902, AS 2124, GC21, or bespoke forms — RFIs, variations, extension-of-time assessments, progress claims, notices, and correspondence. Impartial where the contract requires it.
items.when: You are the principal or superintendent representative and need the paperwork run by a firm that knows both sides of the same disputes.
items.deliverable: Ongoing engagement with monthly reporting; complete document register handed over at practical completion.

items.name: Superintendent Services
items.what: Independent superintendent role: site visits, certifications, extension-of-time determinations, direction to correct, practical completion certification, and DLP administration. Held to the same standard of independence a court would expect.
items.when: You need a superintendent who will hold the middle ground when it costs one party money, and who is prepared to defend a determination in writing.
items.deliverable: Site inspection reports, monthly certificates, formal determinations, PC and DLP certificates.

items.name: Feasibility Studies
items.what: Pre-commitment feasibility: site constraints, cost planning to elemental level, indicative programme, and a risk register you can hand to a board or a bank. Benchmarked against comparable completed projects.
items.when: You are about to seek finance, land at auction, or trigger a stage-two commitment, and the numbers in front of you have not yet been independently tested.
items.deliverable: Written feasibility report, cost plan, risk register, one revision, and presentation to your board or lender.

items.name: Tender & Procurement
items.trigger: Get the right builder onto the right contract.
items.what: Tender documentation, RFP management, tenderer prequalification, tender evaluation to a scoring matrix, and contract-award recommendation. Contract form and special conditions drafted or reviewed.
items.when: You are moving from documentation to construction and want the tender run cleanly enough to defend the award later if it is questioned.
items.deliverable: Tender package, tenderer register, evaluation report with scoring, and a recommendation memo to the principal.

items.name: Risk & Quality Management
items.what: Project risk register development and maintenance, quality plan review, ITP (inspection & test plan) audits during construction, non-conformance tracking, and defect-prevention advice. Site quality audits on request.
items.when: You want an independent set of eyes on quality and risk — separate from the builder's own QA — either continuously or at defined milestones.
items.deliverable: Risk register, quality audit reports, ITP register review, and non-conformance summaries with recommended actions.
